title: Obtaining Concentrated Extract of Lipases from Orange Waste
author: Clarissa Okino-Delgado
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.j3rcqm6
materials: The crude extracts were fractionated through salting out using 60% ammonium sulfate (Ecibra ®) and through dialysis using dialysis tubing cellulose membrane 43mm (Sigma-Aldrich®). The extracts were lyophilized (Liotop® L101) at -60°C for 24 hours after fractionation and frozen until analysis.

The lipase activity was identified through zymography by using MUF-butyrate substrate (Sigma Aldrich ® ). The concentrated extracts were resuspension in Tris buffer (0.05 M, pH 7.4) containing CHAPS (4%) and protease inhibitor (Sigma-Aldrich 1mM); then, they were homogenized in probe and centrifuged. Different polyacrylamide concentrations, ranging from 5 to 15%, were tested in order to prepare the 10% native polyacrylamide gel. The gel was prepared with 4 mL distilled water, 2.5 ml HCl Tris buffer (0.5 M, pH 8.8), 3.35 mL acrylamide/bis-acrylamide (30/0.8%), 5 μL TEMED, and 50 μL ammonium persulfate. Each gel well was added with 20 μL of each sample and the run was performed at 150 volts. After the electrophoresis, the gel was placed in a vessel containing 100 mL Tris buffer (50 mM, pH 8.0), 2% triton X-100 and 10 μM methylumbelliferyl (MUF) -butyrate for 15 min, at 37°C. The bands were analyzed under ultraviolet light (UV) to allow finding lipase in the extracts. The results were expressed as mean ± standard deviation (SD) and analyzed through Tukey test; all pairs of groups were compared through One-Way ANOVA (non-parametric); p <0.05 was considered statistically significant, whereas p <0.0001 was considered highly significant. The bands were quantified in the Image J 1.15 software. The statistical analysis was performed in the GraphPad Prism 6 software.

steps.title: Collect and Package Orange Waste
steps.instruction: Collect approximately 10 pounds of each waste fraction (peel, core, and frit) generated from the in line extraction of Citrus sinensis L. Osbeck Pear variety oranges.

substeps.instruction: Collect fractions manually from the equipment output location
Package and identify each fraction individually

steps.title: Initial Storage and Milling
steps.instruction: Store the packaged samples for 2 days at 5ºC, then mill them mechanically.

substeps.instruction: Mill samples to a particle volume of approximately 0.5 cm3

steps.title: Lyophilize Samples
steps.instruction: Freeze and lyophilize the milled samples using a Liotop® L101 at -60°C for 24 hours.

steps.title: Final Processing and Storage
steps.instruction: Crush the matrices again after lyophilization and store them at approximately 7ºC.

substeps.instruction: Store for up to 6 months until the time of analysis
